abstract.en: What increases without limit is usually the thing nobody is measuring.
abstract.cn: 无限增长的，往往正是没人去计量的那样东西。

examples.en: The number of students increased by nearly a hundred.
examples.cn: 学生人数增加了将近一百。

examples.en: Exercise can increase your energy level.
examples.cn: 锻炼能提高你的精力水平。

examples.en: The company reported an increase in sales.
examples.cn: 公司报告销售额有所增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快死」——人数因疫情快速变化，增长的忧愁里带着个快字。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ crescere（生长）→ increscere（长起来）；同根词有 decrease、increment、crescent、concrete。

sensesIntro.en: Increase says that something grows inside its own frame, and the word then extends from counts to intensity and finally to a noun for a trend.
sensesIntro.cn: increase 说的是某物在自己的框架里长起来，于是从数量扩展到强度，最后成为表示趋势的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the red line in a thermometer climbing notch by notch.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计里的红线一格一格往上爬。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: numbers of things get larger.
branches.cn: 数量线：事物的数目变大。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: someone raises output on purpose.
branches.cn: 行动线：有人有意提高产量。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: pressure and noise swell.
branches.cn: 程度线：压力与噪音一起膨胀。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the rise itself becomes a thing to report.
branches.cn: 名词线：上升本身变成一个可报道的对象。

branches.en: IDIOM LINE: a fixed phrase describes a trend.
branches.cn: 习语线：固定说法描述一种趋势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inward growth and a root for growing, plus a large family of -crease words.
intro.cn: 一个表「向内生长」的拉丁前缀与表示「生长」的词根，加上一族 -crease 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow on, and English took both halves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」，英语把两部分都借了过来。

items.example: the root of increase and decrease
items.exampleCN: increase 与 decrease 的共同词根

definition_en: more and more as time passes
core_image: 台阶一级一级往上，每一级都比前一级更高
scene: 这几年，很多事都在悄悄变得更难。Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
sceneCN: 这里 increasingly 是「越来越」（第 1 个义项：随时间推移程度加深）；句意是学生们越来越担心找工作。

pos.zh: 副词：日益；愈加；日趋

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「增加、增长」，是本词的动词基础
义为「不断增加的」
义为「越来越少地」，与本词相反

senses.title: More and more over time
senses.titleCN: 越来越：随时间不断加深
senses.definition: used with an adjective to show that a quality grows over time
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用，表示某种性质随时间不断增强
senses.example: Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们越来越担心找工作。
senses.why: The -ly adverb keeps the growth of increase and turns it into a rising curve beside another word.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词保留了 increase 的「生长」义，并把它变成紧挨另一个词的上升曲线。

senses.title: Used of a trend, not a single step
senses.titleCN: 日益：用于趋势而非单次变化
senses.definition: describing a gradual shift observed across a period rather than one event
senses.definitionCN: 描述在一段时期内观察到的渐变，而非单次事件
senses.example: The city has become increasingly quiet at night.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市夜里变得日益安静。
senses.why: A single change is described by increase, but only a long drift earns the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 单次变化用 increase 就够，只有长期漂移才配得上这个副词。

senses.title: Used for growing degree in an argument
senses.titleCN: 愈加：在论述中强调程度递进
senses.definition: used to stress that one statement matters more as the argument goes on
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调随着论述推进，某一说法愈发重要
senses.example: It is increasingly hard to defend that view.
senses.exampleCN: 那种观点越来越难以辩护。
senses.why: Writers borrow the adverb to let a claim sound like an approaching tide.
senses.whyCN: 写作者借用这个副词，让论断听起来像渐渐逼近的潮水。

intro.en: Increasingly is increase with the adjective ending -ing and the adverb ending -ly added in Modern English.
intro.cn: increasingly 是 increase 加形容词词尾 -ing、再加副词词尾 -ly 构成的现代英语派生词。

items.en: Crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow into.
items.cn: crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」。

items.en: The verb encresen entered English from French.
items.cn: 动词 encresen 由法语进入英语。

items.en: The present participle increasing began to work as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 increasing 开始充当形容词。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the adverb in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 加 -ly 后，这个副词在十九世纪成型。

items.en: Modern journalism made it a standard word for trends.
items.cn: 现代新闻写作让它成为描述趋势的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the increase stem; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of worsening degree.
note.cn: 形近组共用 increase 词干；近义组收表示程度加深的副词。

entries.definition: To become larger in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「增加」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: Becoming larger over time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不断增加的」。

entries.definition: Less and less as time passes.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「越来越少地」。

entries.definition: Slowly over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐渐地」，重在慢。

entries.definition: In stages, step by step.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐步地」，重在分阶段。

entries.definition: Used with comparatives to mean always more.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，与比较级连用表示「越来越」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the staircase image, the -ly adverb slot and the trend word of news writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借台阶意象、-ly 副词位置与新闻里的趋势表达。

normal.en: Increase plus -ing plus -ly: a growth that never finishes and only describes another word.
normal.cn: increase 加 -ing 再加 -ly：一个永不结束的生长，只用来修饰别的词。

normal.en: It almost never stands alone; it leans on an adjective such as difficult or important.
normal.cn: 它几乎不单独站立，总倚着一个形容词，如 difficult 或 important。

normal.en: If one step is a jump, this word describes the whole staircase.
normal.cn: 如果一步是跳跃，这个词描述的是整座楼梯。

normal.en: Decrease the first letter and the direction of the staircase reverses.
normal.cn: 把首字母换一换，楼梯的方向就反过来。

normal.en: News headlines love it because it reports a drift without naming a cause.
normal.cn: 新闻标题偏爱它，因为它只报道漂移，不指明原因。

abstract.en: Slow change is the only kind the naked eye cannot catch while it happens.
abstract.cn: 缓慢的变化是唯一在发生当下无法被肉眼捕捉的变化。

abstract.en: To say increasingly is to admit that no single instant can show the shift.
abstract.cn: 说「越来越」，等于承认没有任何一个瞬间能显示这次转变。

abstract.en: The adverb measures direction, while the reader still has to guess the speed.
abstract.cn: 这个副词只测方向，速度仍要读者自己去猜。

examples.en: Housing in the city is becoming increasingly expensive.
examples.cn: 这座城市的住房越来越贵。

examples.en: People increasingly work from home.
examples.cn: 人们越来越多地在家办公。

examples.en: It is increasingly rare to see a public phone.
examples.cn: 公共电话越来越少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印快格林里」——印得越来越快，纸一摞摞往格林里堆。

root: 拉丁语 crescere（生长）→ increscere → increase；加 -ing、-ly 构成 increasingly。

sensesIntro.en: Increasingly takes the growth inside increase and turns it into an adverb that always leans on another word and reports a long drift.
sensesIntro.cn: increasingly 把 increase 里的生长变成副词，它总要倚着另一个词，报道的是一段漫长的漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose every step is higher than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座每级都比上一级更高的楼梯。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: a quality deepens beside an adjective.
branches.cn: 性质线：某种性质在形容词旁边加深。

branches.en: PERIOD LINE: the change is spread across years.
branches.cn: 时段线：变化摊展在数年之间。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: a claim gains force as the case goes on.
branches.cn: 论述线：说法随着论证推进而更有力。

branches.en: RHYTHM LINE: the word marks direction, not speed.
branches.cn: 节奏线：这个词标方向，不标速度。

branches.en: TONE LINE: writers use it to sound calm about bad news.
branches.cn: 语气线：写作者用它把坏消息说得平静。

intro.en: A growth root with a participial ending and an adverb ending stacked on top.
intro.cn: 一个「生长」词根上依次叠加分词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere; English added -ing and -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere，英语再加上 -ing 与 -ly。

definition_zh: 难以置信的；惊人的；极好的
definition_en: too strange or extreme to be believed, or extremely good
core_image: 听见一句话，眉毛先跳起来，嘴还没张开
scene: 朋友说自己一夜游过海峡，你第一反应是不信。It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 incredible 是「难以置信的」（第 1 个义项：难以相信）；句意是听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；惊人的；极好的

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信地；极其」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「可信的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式
义为「信任、信用」，与本词同根
义为「可信度」

senses.title: Too strange to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信：奇怪到无法相信
senses.definition: so unusual or extreme that it is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 极其反常或极端，令人难信
senses.example: It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。
senses.why: The Latin credere means to believe, and the negative prefix in- says no: not to be believed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「相信」，否定前缀 in- 说「不」：不可被相信。

senses.title: Extremely large or great
senses.titleCN: 惊人的：规模或程度极大
senses.definition: so great in size or amount that it surprises the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上大到让人吃惊
senses.example: The team worked at incredible speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队以惊人的速度工作。
senses.why: When a number passes belief, the same word measures size rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 当一个数字超出相信的范围，同一个词就转而衡量大小而非真伪。

senses.title: Extremely good, in speech
senses.definition: used informally to praise something as wonderful
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称赞某物好极了
senses.example: The view from the top was incredible.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美极了。
senses.why: Praise borrows the same exclamation: what is beyond belief is also beyond the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 赞叹借用了同一句惊叹：超出相信的，也超出寻常。

senses.title: Hard to accept, used of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 难以接受：形容行为过分
senses.definition: used of behaviour that seems shockingly unfair or careless
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为不公或粗心到令人震惊
senses.example: It is incredible that they left the door unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 他们竟没锁门，真让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix carries moral weight too: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredible comes from Latin incredibilis, from in-, not, and credere, to believe.
intro.cn: incredible 来自拉丁语 incredibilis，由 in-（不）与 credere（相信）构成。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or to entrust, the source of credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，是 credit 与 creed 的来源。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻。

items.en: English borrowed it through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The sense widened from untrue to merely astonishing.
items.cn: 词义从「不真」扩展到「仅仅令人吃惊」。

items.en: Spoken English added the sense of extremely good.
items.cn: 英语口语又添上「极好」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds words of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示「惊异」的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差一个 in-。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」。

entries.definition: Trust that allows buying now and paying later.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、赊账」，同根。

entries.definition: Impossible or very hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，更口语。

entries.definition: So surprising that one is stunned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「惊人的」，重在看后发懵。

entries.definition: Very surprising and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人惊叹的」，偏褒义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the cred-credible pair and the everyday exclamation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、cred/credible 对照与日常惊叹。

normal.en: Credit and creed both hold cred, believe, so incredible means simply not-credible.
normal.cn: credit 与 creed 里都含 cred「相信」，所以 incredible 就是「不可信的」。

normal.en: Take away in- and credible remains, which makes the pair the easiest negative in English.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 剩下 credible，这一对是英语里最好记的否定搭配。

normal.en: When a story is incredible, the eyebrow moves before the mouth does.
normal.cn: 故事令人难以置信时，眉毛先于嘴巴做出反应。

normal.en: The same word praises dinner and prices, because both can pass belief.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸晚饭也形容价格，因为两者都可能超出想象。

normal.en: An incredible amount is not a claim about truth but about the size of the pile.
normal.cn: an incredible amount 不是在说真假，而是在说那一堆有多大。

abstract.en: Belief is the most portable currency: it buys claims, goods and people alike.
abstract.cn: 相信是最通用的货币：它能买到说法、货物与人。

abstract.en: What is incredible is not always false, only unwitnessed.
abstract.cn: 难以置信的不一定假，只是尚未被亲眼看见。

abstract.en: Every wonder starts as a sentence the listener refuses to accept.
abstract.cn: 每一件奇事起初都是一句听者拒绝接受的话。

examples.en: They made an incredible amount of noise.
examples.cn: 他们弄出了惊人的动静。

examples.en: Her recovery was incredible to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她的康复让医生们难以置信。

examples.en: What an incredible meal that was!
examples.cn: 那顿饭真是好极了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德」——因一张信用卡被克扣，账单令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）→ incredibilis；同根词有 credible、credit、credibility、creed、credential。

sensesIntro.en: Incredible begins as the simple denial of belief, then measures size, and finally becomes a spoken word of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: incredible 起初只是对「相信」的简单否定，后来用来衡量大小，最后变成口语中的赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyebrows jumping before the mouth can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴巴还没开口，眉毛先跳了起来。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the tale resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：故事抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a quantity passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：数量越过想象的边界。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: everyday speech turns it into a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：日常口语把它变成褒义词。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is judged too unlikely to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被判为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adjective can be a doubt or a compliment.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个形容词既可是疑问也可是称赞。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending that makes it describable.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，再接形容词词尾，使之可用来形容事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -ibilis, able to be, gave incredibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -ibilis「可……的」，构成 incredibilis。

items.example: the root of credible and credit
items.exampleCN: credible 与 credit 的词根

definition_en: in a way that is very hard to believe, or used to mean extremely
core_image: 一句话说完，听者愣住，时间停了一拍
scene: 听完他说自己一口气跑完马拉松，你半天说不出话。He ran incredibly fast and won the race with ease.
sceneCN: 这里 incredibly 是「极其、非常」（第 3 个义项：程度副词用法）；句意是他跑得快得惊人，轻松赢下比赛。

pos.zh: 副词：难以置信地；极其；非常

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信的」，是本词的基础形容词，去掉 -ly 即成
义为「可信的」，与本词同根，仅差否定前缀
义为「信用、信任」，与本词同含 cred- 词根
义为「可信度」，cred- 词根加名词后缀

senses.title: In a way that is hard to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信地：以令人难信的方式
senses.definition: in a manner that is so unusual that people find it hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 以极其反常、让人难以相信的方式
senses.example: The story ends incredibly, with the hero walking out of the sea alive.
senses.exampleCN: 故事的结局令人难以置信：主人公活着从海里走了出来。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the plain sense of the adjective: an event resists belief, and the word says so.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了形容词的本义：事件抗拒被相信，这个词就直接说出这一点。

senses.title: To a shocking degree of size or amount
senses.titleCN: 惊人到某种规模或数量
senses.definition: used to say that a size, amount, or degree is far beyond what is normal
senses.definitionCN: 表示规模、数量或程度远超寻常
senses.example: The bill was incredibly high after the long phone calls.
senses.exampleCN: 打了那么久的电话后，账单高得吓人。
senses.why: When a quantity passes belief, the word shifts from judging truth to measuring magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 当数量超出相信的范围，这个词就从判断真伪转向衡量大小。

senses.title: Extremely, as an intensifier
senses.titleCN: 极其：程度副词的加强用法
senses.definition: used before an adjective or adverb simply to mean very or extremely
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词或副词前，只表示「非常、极其」
senses.example: She is incredibly kind to strangers who ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 她对前来求助的陌生人极为友善。
senses.why: Daily speech wears the surprise down: what once defied belief now only adds emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把惊异磨平了：曾经表示难以相信，如今只是加强语气。

senses.title: Used of behaviour that is hard to accept
senses.definition: used to describe conduct that seems shockingly careless or unfair
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为粗心或不公到令人震惊
senses.example: They acted incredibly badly by ignoring the complaint for months.
senses.exampleCN: 他们几个月不理投诉，表现得差劲得让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix also carries moral weight: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredibly is the adverb of incredible, from Latin in-, not, and credere, to believe, plus -bilis and the English -ly.
intro.cn: incredibly 是 incredible 的副词形式，源自拉丁语 in-（不）与 credere（相信），加 -bilis，再接英语 -ly。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or entrust, the same root behind credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，与 credit、creed 同根。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels and strange tales.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻异事。

items.en: English borrowed incredible through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入 incredible，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The adverb incredibly appeared, keeping the sense of in a manner hard to believe.
items.cn: 副词 incredibly 出现，保留「以难以相信的方式」之义。

items.en: The sense widened from judging truth to measuring size and degree.
items.cn: 词义从判断真伪扩展到衡量大小与程度。

items.en: Spoken English made it a plain intensifier meaning extremely.
items.cn: 英语口语把它变成普通的程度副词，义为「极其」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of extreme degree.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示极端程度的副词。

entries.definition: Too strange or extreme to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，是本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差否定前缀与词尾。

entries.definition: The quality of not being believable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不可信性」，同根的抽象名词，较罕见。

entries.definition: In a way that is impossible to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」，与 unbelievable 对应，更口语。

entries.definition: To a very high degree, without any surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极其」，只表程度，不带惊异色彩。

entries.definition: In a way that stuns the observer.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「惊人地」，重在看后发懵的反应。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the incredible pair and the everyday intensifier habit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、incredible 对照与日常加强语气的习惯。

normal.en: Incredibly is just incredible with -ly, the standard way English turns adjectives into adverbs.
normal.cn: incredibly 就是 incredible 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变副词的标准做法。

normal.en: Credit holds the root cred, believe, so incredibly is simply not-believably.
normal.cn: credit 里含词根 cred「相信」，所以 incredibly 就是「不可信地」。

normal.en: When someone speaks incredibly, listeners freeze for a beat before answering.
normal.cn: 有人说了难以置信的话时，听者会先愣一拍才接话。

normal.en: Most of the time it only means very, as in incredibly cheap or incredibly kind.
normal.cn: 多数时候它只表示「非常」，如 incredibly cheap（便宜得惊人）、incredibly kind（极为友善）。

normal.en: Swap in extremely and the sentence still works, only the surprise is gone.
normal.cn: 把 extremely 换进去句子照样成立，只是惊异感消失了。

abstract.en: Belief has a doorway, and some facts are simply too wide to fit through it.
abstract.cn: 相信有一道门，有些事实太宽，挤不过去。

abstract.en: Surprise is a debt language repays by turning every strong word into mild praise.
abstract.cn: 惊异是一笔债，语言用「把强烈的词磨成寻常赞美」来偿还。

abstract.en: The loudest intensifier is the one that still remembers being a doubt.
abstract.cn: 最有力的加强词，是还记得自己曾是疑问的那个。

examples.en: The city has grown incredibly quickly over the past decade.
examples.cn: 过去十年这座城市的发展快得惊人。

examples.en: He told the story so incredibly that no one could follow it.
examples.cn: 他把故事讲得离奇至极，没人听得明白。

examples.en: The mountain path is steep and incredibly dangerous in winter.
examples.cn: 这条山径陡峭，冬天危险至极。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德利」——因账单被克扣得离谱，利润（利）令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）+ -bilis（可……的）构成 incredibilis，英语加副词后缀 -ly 得 incredibly；同根词有 incredible、credible、credit、credibility。

sensesIntro.en: Incredibly begins as the adverb of disbelief, then measures size, softens into a plain intensifier, and can still judge conduct.
sensesIntro.cn: incredibly 起初表示难以相信的方式，后来衡量大小，再磨平为普通程度副词，但仍可评判行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pause in the conversation before anyone can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：对话里停了一拍，没人接得上话。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the manner itself resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：方式本身抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a degree passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：程度越过想象的边界。

branches.en: EMPHASIS LINE: daily speech reduces it to a plain very.
branches.cn: 强调线：日常口语把它降为普通的「非常」。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is described as too bad to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被描述为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adverb can carry shock or mere emphasis.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个副词既可承载惊异，也可只是加强语气。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，接形容词词尾，再加英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -bilis, able to be, gave incredibilis; English added -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -bilis「可……的」构成 incredibilis；英语再加 -ly。

items.example: the root of credible and credit
items.exampleCN: credible 与 credit 的词根

items.meaning: in a way that is hard to believe; extremely

definition_en: used to emphasize that something is true, or to add a stronger statement
core_image: 点了点头，又把手按在桌上补一句「真的」
scene: 别人怀疑你的说法时，你会加重语气再确认一次。It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 indeed 是「确实」（第 1 个义项：强调所说的为真）；句意是那确实是全年最冷的一夜。

pos.zh: 副词：确实；的确；实际上

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「行为、事迹」，是本词的后半部分
义为「超过」，与 indeed 的 -ceed 部分形近，注意区分

senses.title: Emphasizing that something is true
senses.definition: used to make a statement stronger or to confirm it
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强或确认某个说法
senses.example: It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 那确实是全年最冷的一夜。
senses.why: The word is literally in deed, in the fact of the matter, so it points at reality itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在事实中」，所以它直接指向现实本身。

senses.title: Adding a stronger point
senses.titleCN: 而且：补上更进一步的说法
senses.definition: used to introduce a further and stronger piece of information
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步、更有力的信息
senses.example: He is a good teacher, indeed a great one.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位好老师，而且是一位了不起的老师。
senses.why: Confirming one fact opens the door to a bigger one, so the word also links escalations.
senses.whyCN: 确认一件事就打开了更大的门，因此这个词也用来连接递进。

senses.title: After very or an adjective, as intensifier
senses.titleCN: 非常：放在形容词后加强程度
senses.definition: placed after very and an adjective to strengthen the description
senses.definitionCN: 放在 very 加形容词之后，加强描述
senses.example: She was very tired indeed.
senses.exampleCN: 她确实非常累。
senses.why: At the end of a phrase the word becomes a stamp of emphasis, almost a nod.
senses.whyCN: 放在短语末尾时，它变成一枚强调的印章，几乎就是一个点头。

senses.title: Showing surprise or interest
senses.titleCN: 真的吗：表示惊讶或兴趣
senses.definition: used in speech to show mild surprise or to invite more talk
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示轻微的惊讶，或邀请对方继续讲
senses.example: Indeed? I had not heard about that.
senses.exampleCN: 真的吗？我还没听说过这事。
senses.why: The same confirmation becomes a question when the voice rises, a common speech habit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个确认词在语调上扬时就成了疑问，这是常见的口语习惯。

intro.en: Indeed is a Middle English compound of in and deed, meaning in fact or in reality.
intro.cn: indeed 是中古英语合成词，由 in 与 deed「行为、事实」构成，意为「在事实上」。

items.en: Dæd meant a deed or an act, the thing actually done.
items.cn: dæd 意为行为或事迹，即实际做出的事。

items.en: In dede was a phrase meaning in fact, written as one word later.
items.cn: in dede 是「事实上」的短语，后来写成一个词。

items.en: The word became a common way to confirm an assertion.
items.cn: 这个词成为确认论断的常用手段。

items.en: It also took the linking sense of a further, stronger point.
items.cn: 它也承担起引出更进一步说法的连接作用。

items.en: Spoken use added the surprised question, spoken with a rising tone.
items.cn: 口语用法又添上带上扬语调的惊讶疑问。

note.en: The look-alike group shares short in- words; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of emphasis and confirmation.
note.cn: 形近组收以 in- 开头的短词；近义组收表示强调与确认的副词。

entries.definition: An action that is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行为、事迹」。

entries.definition: To start a line further from the margin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩进」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: An alphabetical list at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「索引」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: Without doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然、肯定」。

entries.definition: In fact, used to correct a belief.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上」，常用于纠正看法。

entries.definition: In a genuine way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「真正地」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal in-deed reading, the sentence-final stamp and the rising question.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的 in-deed 结构、句末盖章与上扬疑问。

normal.en: In plus deed is in the deed, in what was actually done, so indeed means in fact.
normal.cn: in 加 deed 就是「在行为中」，即在真正做过的事里，所以意为「事实上」。

normal.en: A friend indeed is a friend in deeds, not merely in words, a proverb that explains the word.
normal.cn: a friend indeed 是「在行动上」的朋友而非只在嘴上，这句谚语正好解释这个词。

normal.en: Very tired indeed puts the nod at the end of the sentence.
normal.cn: very tired indeed 把那个点头放在句末。

normal.en: He is good, indeed great: the second statement is a step higher than the first.
normal.cn: He is good, indeed great：后一句比前一句又高了一级。

normal.en: Say it with a rising voice and the same word becomes really?
normal.cn: 把语调扬起来，同一个词就变成了「真的吗？」

abstract.en: Indeed is the shortest form of evidence: it points at the deed instead of describing it.
abstract.cn: indeed 是最短的证据形式：它指向行为，而不描述行为。

abstract.en: To confirm is a social act, so the word always assumes someone who doubted.
abstract.cn: 确认是一种社交行为，所以这个词总预设了一个曾怀疑的人。

abstract.en: A sentence ending in indeed leaves no room for the listener to disagree quietly.
abstract.cn: 以 indeed 收尾的句子，不留给听者悄悄反对的余地。

examples.en: Thank you very much indeed.
examples.cn: 真是非常感谢。

examples.en: The task was hard, indeed almost impossible.
examples.cn: 这项任务很难，几乎不可能完成。

examples.en: Indeed, the plan worked better than we hoped.
examples.cn: 的确，这计划比我们预想的更成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印底的」——印在纸底的那行字，的确是证据。

root: 中古英语 in（在）+ deed（行为、事实）→ in dede（事实上）→ indeed。

sensesIntro.en: Indeed starts as a pointer to a deed, becomes a stamp of truth, then a step up in argument, a sentence-final intensifier and finally a surprised question.
sensesIntro.cn: indeed 起初指向「行为」，后来成为真实的印章，再变成论述中的递进、句末的加强，最后成了惊讶的疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod of the head, then a hand pressed flat on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：先点头，再把手平按在桌上。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the word points at what really happened.
branches.cn: 真实线：这个词指向真正发生的事。

branches.en: ESCALATION LINE: the next claim goes one step further.
branches.cn: 递进线：下一个说法再进一层。

branches.en: STAMP LINE: placed after an adjective, it seals the description.
branches.cn: 盖章线：放在形容词后，为描述封口。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: a rising tone turns it into a question.
branches.cn: 口语线：上扬的语调把它变成疑问。

branches.en: RHETORIC LINE: confirming first makes a bigger claim easier to accept.
branches.cn: 修辞线：先确认小事，大话更容易被接受。

intro.en: A preposition fused with an Old English noun of action, plus a short family of -deed words.
intro.cn: 一个介词与一个古英语行为名词熔成一词，外加一族简短的 -deed 词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalent structure is in facto, in the fact, which also gives English fact and feat.
latinIntro.cn: 对应的拉丁结构是 in facto「在事实中」，英语由此得到 fact 与 feat。

items.example: He said so, and indeed so it was.
items.exampleCN: 他这么说，事实也确是如此。

items.meaning: in action, not only in words
items.meaningCN: 在行动上，而不只在口头上
items.example: help in deed as well as in word

items.meaning: a document that transfers a gift

definition_en: freedom from control by another person, group or country
core_image: 一只鸟第一次不再靠着巢沿，自己张开翅膀
scene: 搬出父母家，才真正懂得独立是什么味道。Living alone taught her independence.
sceneCN: 这里 independence 是「独立」（第 1 个义项：不依赖他人）；句意是独自生活教会了她独立。

pos.zh: 名词：独立；自主；不受支配

derivatives.zh: 义为「独立的」，是本词的形容词形式
义为「独立地」
义为「依赖」，去掉 in- 即成相反名词
义为「依靠」，与本词同根

senses.title: Freedom from another's control
senses.definition: the state of not being controlled or supported by another person
senses.definitionCN: 不被他人控制或供养的状态
senses.example: Living alone taught her independence.
senses.exampleCN: 独自生活教会了她独立。
senses.why: The word is in- not plus depend, to hang from, so independence means not hanging from anyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 in-（不）加 depend（悬靠），所以独立就是不再挂在任何人身上。

senses.title: A nation's self-rule
senses.definition: the freedom of a country to govern itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家自行治理的自由
senses.example: The country declared independence in nineteen sixty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一九六零年宣布独立。
senses.why: Politics simply lifts the personal image to the scale of a whole people.
senses.whyCN: 政治只是把个人的意象放大到整个民族的尺度。

senses.title: Money that needs no patron
senses.titleCN: 经济独立：不靠他人供养
senses.definition: having enough income to live without help from others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够收入、无需他人帮助也能生活
senses.example: A part-time job gave him financial independence.
senses.exampleCN: 一份兼职让他经济上独立了。
senses.why: Money is the modern rope that ties people to each other, so cutting it makes them independent.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是现代社会把人系在一起的绳索，剪断它人便独立了。

senses.title: Separateness in thought or method
senses.titleCN: 独立性：思想或方法上自成一体
senses.definition: the quality of forming one's own judgement rather than copying others
senses.definitionCN: 形成自己的判断而非照搬他人的品质
senses.example: Her research shows real independence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究显示出真正的思想独立性。
senses.why: Beyond bodies and borders, the word describes a mind that does not lean on another.
senses.whyCN: 除了身体与国界，这个词还形容一颗不倚靠别人的心。

intro.en: Independence is in-, not, plus dependence, from Latin dependere, to hang from.
intro.cn: independence 是 in-（不）加 dependence，后者源自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from something, from de- and pendere.
items.cn: dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂」，由 de- 与 pendere 构成。

items.en: Depend entered English with the sense of being supported by another.
items.cn: depend 进入英语时带有「依靠他人支撑」之义。

items.en: Independence appeared in the seventeenth century for freedom from control.
items.cn: independence 在十七世纪出现，表示不受控制。

items.en: Political use spread after the American Declaration in seventeen seventy-six.
items.cn: 一七七六年美国《独立宣言》之后，政治用法广泛流传。

items.en: Personal and financial senses grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 个人与经济层面的义项在十九、二十世纪发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hang root; the near-meaning group holds words of freedom and self-rule.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「悬挂」的 pend- 词根；近义组收表示自由与自决的词。

entries.definition: Free from control by others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独立的」。

entries.definition: The state of needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依赖」。

entries.definition: A person who depends on another by custom or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受抚养者」。

entries.definition: The power to act as one wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自由」。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自治」，多为术语。

entries.definition: Reliance on one's own powers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自力更生」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the hanging root, the bird leaving the nest and the declaration of independence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「悬挂」词根、离巢的鸟与独立宣言。

normal.en: Depend is to hang down from someone, so independence is the moment the hook is removed.
normal.cn: depend 是挂在某人身上，那么独立就是钩子被取下的时刻。

normal.en: The verb is depend, the adjective independent, the noun independence: only the ending changes.
normal.cn: 动词 depend、形容词 independent、名词 independence，只换词尾。

normal.en: Dependence and independence face each other with one small in- between.
normal.cn: dependence 与 independence 只隔一个小小的 in-。

normal.en: A baby bird at the nest edge is the best picture: first it flaps, then it lets go.
normal.cn: 巢沿的雏鸟是最好的画面：先扇翅，再放手。

normal.en: Independence Day celebrates a document that ended a hanging rope across the ocean.
normal.cn: 独立日纪念的是一纸文书，它剪断了横跨大洋的那根绳。

abstract.en: Independence is measured not by who you leave but by who no longer has to carry you.
abstract.cn: 独立不看离开了谁，而看谁不必再把你背着。

abstract.en: True autonomy keeps the link but gives it a looser knot.
abstract.cn: 真正的自主保留联结，只把绳结放松。

abstract.en: A mind that never leans will never know what it believes.
abstract.cn: 从不倚靠的心，也不会知道自己相信什么。

examples.en: She values her independence more than a big salary.
examples.cn: 比起高薪，她更看重自己的独立。

examples.en: The colony fought for independence.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地曾为独立而战。

examples.en: Learning to cook is a first step towards independence.
examples.cn: 学会做饭是迈向独立的第一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地盆等次」——自己占地印盆，不必等别人赏赐，便是独立。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dependere（悬挂于，来自 de- + pendere「悬挂」）→ independence；同根词有 depend、dependent、pendant、suspend。

sensesIntro.en: Independence begins as the removal of an outer hook, then scales to a country's self-rule, to money without a patron, and to a mind that judges for itself.
sensesIntro.cn: independence 起初是不再挂在钩上，而后扩展到国家的自主、无须供养人的财富，以及自做判断的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young bird letting go of the nest edge on its first flight.
core.cn: 核心意象：雏鸟第一次放手离巢。

branches.en: PERSONAL LINE: no one else gives the orders.
branches.cn: 个人线：不再由他人发号令。

branches.en: POLITICAL LINE: a country governs itself.
branches.cn: 政治线：国家自行治理。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: income arrives without a patron.
branches.cn: 金钱线：收入不必来自恩主。

branches.en: MIND LINE: judgement is formed alone.
branches.cn: 思想线：判断由自己形成。

branches.en: GROWTH LINE: independence is usually won step by step.
branches.cn: 成长线：独立往往一步一步赢来。

intro.en: A negative prefix, a prefix meaning down, a root meaning hang and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀、一个表示「向下」的前缀、一个意为「悬挂」的词根，以及一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang, with de-, down, gave dependere, to hang from; in- then denies it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 de-「向下」成为 dependere「悬于」，再加 in- 加以否定。

items.example: the root of suspend and pendant
items.exampleCN: suspend 与 pendant 的词根

items.meaning: to hang from, to rely on
state of not hanging from others
to hang up, to stop for a time

definition_zh: 独立的；自主的；不相关的
definition_en: not controlled by or relying on other people or things
core_image: 两根柱子之间没有横梁相连，各自立着
scene: 两个人可以意见不同，却依旧是朋友。She is independent enough to make her own decision.
sceneCN: 这里 independent 是「独立的」（第 1 个义项：自主做决定）；句意是她足够独立，能自己做决定。

pos.zh: 形容词：独立的；自主的；不相关的
名词：无党派人士（少见）

derivatives.zh: 义为「独立地」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「独立、自主」
义为「依赖的」，去掉 in- 即成相反形式
义为「依靠」，与本词同根

senses.title: Able to act or decide alone
senses.titleCN: 独立的：能自主行动或决定
senses.definition: able to do things or make decisions without help from others
senses.definitionCN: 能够不需他人帮助做事或做决定
senses.example: She is independent enough to make her own decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她足够独立，能自己做决定。
senses.why: The stem depend means to hang from; the prefix in- says the hanging has been cut.
senses.whyCN: 词干 depend 意为「悬挂于」，前缀 in- 表示那根挂绳已被剪断。

senses.title: Not ruled by another country
senses.titleCN: 国家独立：不受他国统治
senses.definition: governing itself rather than being ruled from outside
senses.definitionCN: 自行治理而不受外部统治
senses.example: The island became independent in nineteen eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛在一九八零年独立。
senses.why: Politics uses the same image at the scale of a whole territory.
senses.whyCN: 政治在整片领土的尺度上使用同一意象。

senses.title: Not connected or affected by
senses.definition: not depending on something else for its value or truth
senses.definitionCN: 其价值或真实性不取决于其他事物
senses.example: The two results are independent of each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个结果彼此无关。
senses.why: In mathematics and science, no hang means no link: one quantity does not move the other.
senses.whyCN: 在数学与科学里，不「挂」就是无关联：一个量不会带动另一个量。

senses.title: Not belonging to a party or company
senses.titleCN: 独立的：不属于党派或机构
senses.definition: not controlled by a political party, a company or a large organization
senses.definitionCN: 不受政党、公司或大型机构控制
senses.example: The report was written by an independent expert.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告由一位独立专家撰写。
senses.why: Freedom from an owner is valued as impartiality, so the word turns into a guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱所有者被视为公正，于是这个词本身成了一种保证。

senses.title: As a noun, one who is unaffiliated
senses.definition: a person who does not belong to a political party
senses.definitionCN: 不属于任何政党的人
senses.example: Two independents hold the balance in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 两名无党派人士在议会中掌握关键票数。
senses.why: A shorthand grew from the adjective: no party label, so simply an independent.
senses.whyCN: 从形容词缩出一个名词：没有党籍标签，就叫 independent。

intro.en: Independent joins in-, not, to dependent, from Latin dependere, to hang from.
intro.cn: independent 把否定前缀 in- 加到 dependent 之上，后者源自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, and dependere meant to hang down from something.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂」。

items.en: Ecclesiastical writers formed independentia for freedom from another's rule.
items.cn: 教会作家造出 independentia，表示不依附于他人统治。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Political and scientific uses made it a general word for no dependence.
items.cn: 政治与科学用法使它成为泛指「无依赖」的词。

items.en: The noun for an unaffiliated member of parliament appeared in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 指无党派议员的名词用法在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hang root; the near-meaning group holds words of acting alone.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「悬挂」的 pend- 词根；近义组收表示独立行事的词。

entries.definition: The state of being free of control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「独立」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: Needing someone or something else.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「依赖的」，去掉 in- 即成。

entries.definition: A hanging ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吊坠」，同根。

entries.definition: Not joined to others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「分开的、单独的」。

entries.definition: Working for oneself rather than an employer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自雇的」。

entries.definition: Not supporting either side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中立的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the cut rope, the variant endings and the scientific sense of independence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借剪断的绳子、词尾变化与科学里的独立。

normal.en: Depend plus in-, and the hanging rope is cut; nothing above holds you any more.
normal.cn: depend 加 in-，挂绳被剪断，上面再没有东西提着你。

normal.en: Independent of is the scientific spelling of no connection between two variables.
normal.cn: independent of 是科学里「两个变量无关联」的说法。

normal.en: The adjective ends in -ent, the noun in -ence: one letter keeps the family together.
normal.cn: 形容词以 -ent 结尾，名词以 -ence 结尾，一个字母维系着这家人。

normal.en: An independent voter stands between two columns, touching neither.
normal.cn: 独立选民站在两根柱子之间，谁也不扶。

normal.en: Independent films are made without a big studio hanging over the director.
normal.cn: 独立电影是在没有大制片厂压着导演的情况下拍出来的。

abstract.en: Independence is a relation described by its absence: freedom from someone, not freedom in general.
abstract.cn: 独立是一个由「缺席」描述的关系：相对于某人的自由，而非笼统的自由。

abstract.en: To be independent is to carry one's own weight, which is also to feel it.
abstract.cn: 独立就是自己承担重量，也就要感到那份重量。

abstract.en: Science charges a high price for independence: nothing may be taken on trust.
abstract.cn: 科学为独立付出高昂代价：任何事都不许只凭信任接受。

examples.en: The children grew more independent as they got older.
examples.cn: 孩子们长大后越来越独立。

examples.en: Her decision was independent of mine.
examples.cn: 她的决定与我无关。

examples.en: He works as an independent consultant.
examples.cn: 他做独立顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地盆登特」——自己印地、自己有盆，抬头登上高处，不靠别人。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ depend （de- + pendere「悬挂」）→ independent；同根词有 depend、dependence、suspend、pendant。

sensesIntro.en: Independent denies hanging from another, and the denial stretches from a person to a country, to a variable, to an organization and finally to a person without a party.
sensesIntro.cn: independent 否定「挂在别处」，这一否定从人扩展到国家、变量、机构，最后落成没有党籍的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pillars standing without any beam between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根柱子各自立着，中间没有横梁。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: decisions are made without help.
branches.cn: 个人线：决定无需他人帮助。

branches.en: STATE LINE: a territory governs itself.
branches.cn: 国家线：领土自行治理。

branches.en: SCIENCE LINE: no variable moves another.
branches.cn: 科学线：没有变量牵动另一个。

branches.en: INSTITUTION LINE: no party or company owns the work.
branches.cn: 机构线：作品不属于党派或公司。

branches.en: POLITICS LINE: a label becomes a person.
branches.cn: 政治线：一个标签变成了一类人。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a compound of down and hang, plus an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加在「向下 + 悬挂」的合成词上，再接形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang, with de-, down, and the negative in-, gave independentem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 de-「向下」，再加否定 in-，构成 independentem。

definition_en: an alphabetical list at the end of a book, or a number that shows a level or change
core_image: 一根食指，指着书后的字母表，告诉你从哪一页找起
scene: 查资料时，先翻书末的索引比一页页读快得多。Look it up in the index at the back of the book.
sceneCN: 这里 index 是「索引」（第 1 个义项：书末按字母排列的条目表）；句意是到书后的索引里查一下。

pos.zh: 名词：索引；指数；指标；食指
动词：为……编索引；把……列为指标

derivatives.zh: 义为「指数化」，指工资等按指数调整
义为「与指数挂钩的、附有索引的」
义为「编索引的人」

senses.title: A list pointing to pages
senses.definition: an alphabetical list of names or subjects with the pages where they appear
senses.definitionCN: 按字母排列的名称或主题表，并注明出现页码
senses.example: Look it up in the index at the back of the book.
senses.exampleCN: 到书后的索引里查一下。
senses.why: Latin index meant the finger that points, and a list of pointers is the same gesture in print.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 index 意为「指点的食指」，而一串指路的条目正是同一手势印在纸上。

senses.title: A number showing a level
senses.definition: a number that measures changes in prices, wages or production compared with a base
senses.definitionCN: 与基期相比，衡量价格、工资或产量变化的数字
senses.example: The price index rose again last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月物价指数又上涨了。
senses.why: A single number points to the state of a larger system, so economics borrowed the pointer.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字指向更大系统的状况，经济学于是借用了这根指头。

senses.title: A sign of something else
senses.definition: something that shows the level or condition of another thing
senses.definitionCN: 能显示另一事物水平或状况的东西
senses.example: Handwriting is a poor index of character.
senses.exampleCN: 笔迹不是反映性格的好指标。
senses.why: Any sign can point the way the finger does, so the word widens to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 任何迹象都能像食指那样指点方向，于是词义扩展到「证据」。

senses.title: The finger that points
senses.definition: the finger next to the thumb, used for pointing
senses.definitionCN: 拇指旁用来指点的指头
senses.example: He cut his index finger on a page.
senses.exampleCN: 他的食指被书页划破了。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives in the fixed phrase index finger, a trace of the word's birth.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项保存在 index finger 这个固定搭配里，留下词诞生的痕迹。

senses.title: To make an index, as a verb
senses.definition: to prepare an index for a book or to record items in one
senses.definitionCN: 为书编索引，或把条目录入索引
senses.example: The archive has indexed every letter.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆已为每封信编了索引。
senses.why: Once the noun exists, the verb simply says what one does with it.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦存在，动词只需说明拿它做什么。

intro.en: Index is Latin for a pointer or forefinger, from indicare, to point out.
intro.cn: index 是拉丁语中「指点者、食指」一词，源自 indicare「指出」。

items.en: Index meant the finger that points and also a sign or informer.
items.cn: index 指指点的食指，也指标志或告发者。

items.en: A title in a book was called an index because it pointed to chapters.
items.cn: 书的标题被称为 index，因为它指向各章。

items.en: Printing gave index the modern sense of an alphabetical list of pages.
items.cn: 印刷术赋予 index 现代含义：按字母排列的页码表。

items.en: Politics borrowed it for the Index of banned books.
items.cn: 政治借它指代「禁书目录」（Index）。

items.en: Statistics gave it the sense of a measuring number.
items.cn: 统计学又给了它「衡量数字」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds words for lists and measures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示目录与度量的词。

entries.definition: To show or point out something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表明、指示」，同根。

entries.definition: The classical plural of index.
entries.definitionCN: index 的拉丁式复数。

entries.definition: To start a line further from the margin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩进」，与 index 形近。

entries.definition: The list of chapters at the front of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目录」，在书前。

entries.definition: A sign that shows a level or change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指标、指示物」。

entries.definition: An ordered list of items for reference.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目录、编目」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pointing finger, the split plural and the stock market index.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借指点的食指、双重复数与股市指数。

normal.en: The index finger and the book index are the same word: both point where to look.
normal.cn: index finger 与书里的索引是同一个词：两者都指向该看的地方。

normal.en: Two plurals exist: indexes for lists and indices in science, as Latin once had it.
normal.cn: 它有两个复数：目录用 indexes，科学用 indices，沿用拉丁旧形。

normal.en: The Shanghai Composite is an index because one number points at hundreds of shares.
normal.cn: 上证指数之所以叫 index，是因为一个数字指向成百上千只股票。

normal.en: Contents tells you what chapters there are; index tells you where a word hides.
normal.cn: contents 告诉你有哪些章，index 告诉你某个词藏在哪。

normal.en: A poor index of character: a sign points at something without being that thing.
normal.cn: a poor index of character：标志指向某物，却并不等于该物。

abstract.en: To index is to decide in advance which words will be findable later.
abstract.cn: 编索引就是预先决定日后哪些词能被找到。

abstract.en: An index is a map of a book, and every map lies about something.
abstract.cn: 索引是一本书的地图，而每张地图都在某处有所隐瞒。

abstract.en: A single number that stands for a whole system always hides the disagreements inside it.
abstract.cn: 用一个数字代表整个系统，必然隐藏了其中的分歧。

examples.en: The report includes an index of names.
examples.cn: 报告附有一份人名索引。

examples.en: The consumer price index fell slightly.
examples.cn: 消费物价指数略有下降。

examples.en: She pointed with her index finger at the map.
examples.cn: 她用食指点着地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印得克斯」——印刷时把条目印得整齐，还得配上索引。

root: 拉丁语 index（指点者、食指），源自 indicare（指出，由 in- + dic-「说」构成）；同根词有 indicate、dictate、dictionary、contradict。

sensesIntro.en: Index starts as a pointing finger, turns into a printed list of pointers, then into a number that points at a system, then into any sign at all, and finally into the act of making such a list.
sensesIntro.cn: index 起于指点的食指，转为纸上的指路表，再转为指向系统的数字，继而泛指任何标志，最后成为「编索引」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a forefinger pointing at a lettered list behind the book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根食指指着书后按字母排列的表。

branches.en: BOOK LINE: a list points to pages.
branches.cn: 书本线：一份表指向各页。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: one figure points at an economy.
branches.cn: 数字线：一个数字指向整个经济。

branches.en: EVIDENCE LINE: any sign can point at a condition.
branches.cn: 证据线：任何迹象都能指向某种状况。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the pointing finger keeps the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 身体线：指点的食指保留着最古老的义项。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: to index is to build the pointing list.
branches.cn: 动作线：编索引就是造出那张指路的表。

intro.en: A Latin root for pointing and saying, with a noun ending meaning one who does.
intro.cn: 一个意为「指出、说出」的拉丁词根，加一个表示「做某事者」的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin indicare, to point out, with -ex, produced index, one who points.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 indicare「指出」加 -ex，构成 index「指点者」。

items.example: the root of dictate and dictionary
items.exampleCN: dictate 与 dictionary 的词根

items.meaning: to say aloud for another to write

definition_en: to show that something exists or is likely, or to point it out
core_image: 手指在图纸上轻轻一点，示意某项出了问题
scene: 仪表盘上亮起红灯，说明发动机可能过热。The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
sceneCN: 这里 indicate 是「显示」（第 1 个义项：表明某种情况存在）；句意是仪表显示温度突然升高。

pos.zh: 动词：表明；显示；指出；暗示

derivatives.zh: 义为「迹象、指示」，由本词加 -ion 构成
义为「指标、指示器」
义为「表明的、暗示的」，常与 of 连用
义为「索引、指标」，与本词同根

senses.title: To show as a sign
senses.titleCN: 表明：作为某种情况的标志
senses.definition: to show that a state or event exists
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某种状况或事件存在
senses.example: The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 仪表显示温度突然升高。
senses.why: The Latin dicare means to make known, and in- points the gesture at something specific.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dicare 意为「使之知晓」，in- 则把这个动作指向具体对象。

senses.title: To point out directly
senses.definition: to show a thing to someone by pointing or naming it
senses.definitionCN: 通过指点或说出名称来把某物显示给人
senses.example: He indicated the seat beside him.
senses.exampleCN: 他指了指身边的座位。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical: a finger makes the message known without words.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是具体的：一根手指不动嘴就把信息告知了。

senses.title: To suggest without saying
senses.definition: to make a wish or opinion known indirectly
senses.definitionCN: 间接地表露愿望或看法
senses.example: She indicated that she would rather stay.
senses.exampleCN: 她暗示自己宁可留下。
senses.why: A point can be polite as well as clear: the finger moves, the sentence remains unsaid.
senses.whyCN: 一指既可清晰也可含蓄：手指动了，话却没说出口。

senses.title: To be a sign of, of data
senses.titleCN: 表明：数据与研究中的用法
senses.definition: used of facts or studies to show what they suggest
senses.definitionCN: 用于事实或研究，表示其暗示的结论
senses.example: The results indicate that the method works.
senses.exampleCN: 结果表明这个方法有效。
senses.why: Research cannot speak, so the verb lets numbers point at a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 研究本身不会说话，这个动词让数字指向一个结论。

senses.title: To signal on a vehicle
senses.titleCN: 打转向灯：车辆上的指示
senses.definition: to signal an intention to turn, using lights on a car
senses.definitionCN: 用汽车灯示意即将转向
senses.example: Always indicate before you turn.
senses.exampleCN: 转弯前一定要打转向灯。
senses.why: A machine repeats the gesture for you, so the word replaces the verb signal in British usage.
senses.whyCN: 机器代替人做这个手势，于是英式英语用这个词代替 signal。

intro.en: Indicate comes from Latin indicare, to point out, from in- and dicare, to make known.
intro.cn: indicate 来自拉丁语 indicare「指出」，由 in- 与 dicare「使之知晓」构成。

items.en: Dicare meant to proclaim or dedicate, from the same family as dicere, to say.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告或奉献，与 dicere「说」同族。

items.en: Indicare meant to point out or show, often with a gesture.
items.cn: indicare 意为指出或显示，常伴手势。

items.en: English borrowed it to describe signs and measurements.
items.cn: 英语借它描述标志与测量结果。

items.en: The verb became a standard word in reports of data.
items.cn: 这个词成为报告数据时的标准用词。

items.en: British English made it the everyday word for signalling in a car.
items.cn: 英式英语让它成为汽车打转向灯的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示「显示」的动词。

entries.definition: A sign that something exists.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迹象、指示」。

entries.definition: A gauge or sign that shows a level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指示器、指标」。

entries.definition: To give time or effort to a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「奉献」，与 indicate 形近。

entries.definition: To make something visible or clear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「显示」，最通用。

entries.definition: To make someone think something is likely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示、表明」，语气更弱。

entries.definition: To make known something hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「揭示」，强调原本隐藏。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pointing gesture, the dictionary root and the turn signal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借指点的手势、dictionary 词根与转向灯。

normal.en: Dictionary and dictate share the root to say; indicate is the root plus in, saying towards a thing.
normal.cn: dictionary 与 dictate 共有「说」的词根；indicate 就是该词根加 in，朝着某物说话。

normal.en: Indicate that is the standard opening of any scientific finding.
normal.cn: indicate that 是一切科学结论的标准开头。

normal.en: Indicate the seat: a finger does the work of a whole sentence.
normal.cn: indicate the seat：一根手指干完了一整句话的活。

normal.en: In British cars, indicate is written on the turn signal lever's job description.
normal.cn: 在英国车里，转向灯杆的职责就用 indicate 来写。

normal.en: Indication, indicator, indicative: the ending changes but the pointing stays.
normal.cn: indication、indicator、indicative：词尾在变，指点的动作不变。

abstract.en: To indicate is to stay one step short of proof, and careful writers keep that step.
abstract.cn: 表明离证明还差一步，谨慎的写作者会守住这一步。

abstract.en: A sign is always smaller than the thing it points to.
abstract.cn: 标志永远比它所指向的东西小。

abstract.en: Language indicates before it states, and most arguments turn on that gap.
abstract.cn: 语言先暗示再陈述，多数争论就出在这道缝隙上。

examples.en: The map indicates where the river bends.
examples.cn: 地图标出了河流拐弯的地方。

examples.en: Early studies indicated a strong link.
examples.cn: 早期研究显示出很强的关联。

examples.en: He indicated with a nod that he agreed.
examples.cn: 他点头表示同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地开的」——地图印得清楚，标示该走的方向。

root: 拉丁语 in-（朝向）+ dicare（使之知晓，源自 dicere「说」）→ indicare（指出）；同根词有 index、indication、dedicate、dictate、dictionary。

sensesIntro.en: Indicate begins as a finger making a thing known, then covers any sign, indirect hints, research findings and finally a car's signal lamp.
sensesIntro.cn: indicate 起于手指把某物点明，随后涵盖任何标志、间接暗示、研究结论，最后还指汽车上的信号灯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping a blueprint to show where the fault lies.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在图纸上轻点，示出故障所在。

branches.en: SIGN LINE: readings and results point at a condition.
branches.cn: 标志线：读数与结果指向某种状况。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: a hand shows the object itself.
branches.cn: 手势线：手直接示出对象。

branches.en: POLITENESS LINE: a wish is expressed without words.
branches.cn: 委婉线：愿望不必说出口。

branches.en: DATA LINE: numbers point at a conclusion.
branches.cn: 数据线：数字指向一个结论。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a lamp repeats the gesture for the driver.
branches.cn: 机器线：一盏灯替司机重复这个手势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for pointing at, a root for making known, and a verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示「指向」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「使之知晓」的词根，以及一个动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, upon, plus dicare, to make known, plus -are gave indicare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「朝向」加 dicare「使之知晓」加 -are，构成 indicare。

items.meaning: the act or sign of pointing
